inclusion_rule: Recognizers of phones, words or sentences as text from non-acoustic speech-production signals measured on the speaker (surface EMG, ultrasound, EMA/PMA, EPG, radar, neural recordings), classified by acoustic-model unit design: context-independent phone or word units; context-dependent phone units (triphones, decision-tree clustered); phonetic or articulatory feature (PF/AF) detectors combined with phone models as parallel streams; and data-driven bundling of interdependent PFs into clustered feature models. Boundary: acoustic-input recognizers (the acoustic-ASR AF lineage the target cites), lip-video-only recognizers, AF prediction with no word or phone recognizer, perception studies and reviews are excluded; versions count once. Dated population reused from the published M06/articulatory-signal-speech-recognizer table (12 prior unique studies before 2009-06).

usual_approach.design: phone or word units with no phonetic-feature stream, at the target time (2009-12); feature streams 4 (1 confirmed), bundled 0
usual_approach.note: dated: 10 of 14 prior unique non-acoustic recognizers name no PF/AF stream (pattern match); feature streams confirmed only in Jou 2007; bundled PFs in none; acoustic-ASR precedents named by the target are outside the count and decide the verdict (see dated_counts.acoustic_asr_lineage)

read_fulltext.quote: Since the training set is very small, we only trained context-independent acoustic models.
The stream architecture employs a list of parallel feature streams, each of which contains one of the acoustic or articulatory features.
we ﬁxed the AF sequence and applied them on the test subset.
To analyze the recognition with sub-word units, we tested three unit types with and without context dependency: word units, syllables and phonemes were explored.
The overall average performance of the context-independent system has a WER of 68.92%, which by context-dependent modeling drops to 60.97%.
28.8% to 12.2% in the Gaddy (2020) benchmark dataset for silent speech on an open vocabulary.
continuous HMM (monophone only, due to our dataset size)

dated_counts.tier: pattern match (full text), unique studies; confirmed for the 4 read priors
dated_counts.bundling_fulltext_pattern: all 24 full-text hits on PF bundling (whole wiki) are the target, Schultz-lab papers citing it, surveys citing it, or a neuroscience paper using 'bundles' in the linguistic sense; none is prior
dated_counts.feature_streams_note: pattern hits: Wrench 2000, Maier-Hein 2005, Jou 2007, Meltzner 2008 (Meltzner only through a cited title); confirmed by reading in Jou 2007 only
dated_counts.hmm_note: Suppes 1997 (EEG) and Manabe 2003 (EMG vowels) use no HMM
dated_counts.acoustic_asr_lineage: Outside the setting (acoustic input) and named through the target's citations: PF streams in acoustic ASR (Kirchhoff 1999; Metze and Waibel 2002; Metze 2005), decision-tree clustering (Bahl et al. 1991), and Yu and Schultz 2003 (Eurospeech; not in the wiki), which the target calls similar to its one-stream BDPF (Sec. 3.4) and as already showing the added flexibility of the clustering (Sec. 4). Under the any-signal precedent rule this unread prior blocks an ahead verdict.
